title: Nature Medicine series on real-world clinical AI deployment
key_facts: Nature Medicine published a collection of articles on lessons from deploying AI in real healthcare settings.
Its framing: success depends on workflow integration, human-AI collaboration, trust and patient outcomes, not just algorithm performance.
A Kenyan primary-care cluster trial found ChatGPT-4o decision support did not significantly reduce 14-day treatment failure.
A breast cancer screening trial found automated AI triage was not noninferior to double reading.
Retina4IRD reached 88.5% accuracy for inherited retinal disease diagnosis in a randomized trial.
A study of 1,298 participants found people assisted by an LLM did worse than the LLM alone on ten medical scenarios.
An evaluation of 810 conversations found chatbots often amplify simulated users' psychological vulnerabilities.
quote_evidence: Across all settings the message is largely the same: success in clinical AI depends on more than algorithmic performance.
A pragmatic cluster-randomized trial found that ChatGPT-4o-assisted decision support in Kenyan primary care facilities did not significantly reduce 14-day treatment failure over usual care.

The breast cancer screening trial found that using automated artificial intelligence to triage and support decisions in mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis was not noninferior to double reading.
why_it_matters_hint: The collection shows that clinical AI often does not beat usual care in real-world trials, so evidence matters more than benchmark scores.
